Nand Kishore & Ors . In the matter of : Kriti Kishore & Krity Kishore (Injured) D/o Sh. Naval Kishore R/o Flat No. 802, Arawali Apartment, Kaushambi, Ghaziabad, U.P. -Petiti Versus 1. Nand Kishore (Driver-cum-owner of Hydra Crane No. Hr-55V-4780 and owner of Hydra Crane No. Hr-99Xbt-4138) S/o Sh. Kashi Nath R/o F-107, Village Ghazipur, Delhi. 2. Satender Singh Yadav (Driver of Hydra Crane No. Hr-99Xbt-4138) S/o Sh. Ram Nath R/o F-107, Village Ghazipur, Delhi. 3.Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd. (Insurer of Vehicle No. Hr- 55V-4780) Fai Building 10, Shaeed Jeet Singh Marg, Qutub Institutional Area, New Delhi. -Respondents Date of institution : 05.01.2018 Date of reserve of order : Not reserved Date of Award : 19.07.2024 Awar D 1.
texts.facts: By this award, the claim petition bearing MACP No.188/19 seeking compensation under Sections 166 (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, arising out of the accident, based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) would be decided. 2. Briefly stated facts as per the FIR are that on 29.08.2017 at about 6:50 pm, the petitioner was coming back to her house at Arawali Apartment, Kaushambi, Ghaziabad, U.P. from her office via National Highway-24, Ghazipur, Delhi on her scooty bearing registration No DL-7SBD-9244. It is further stated that the petitioner took turn from flyover circle of Ghazipur Murga Mandi towards EDM Mall, Kaushambi, Ghaziabad, U.P. and at that time, two hydra cranes bearing registration No. Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/ 1 HR-55V-4780 and HR-99XBT-4138 were carrying a big stone without following the public safety and safeguards or blocking of the road there. While the petitioner passed by therefrom, one crane bearing registration No HR-55V-4780 came over the petitioner, as a result of which, petitioner fell down on road alongside her scooty and weight loading part of the crane fell down over the right hand of the petitioner and smashed her right hand. FIR bearing no. 313/17 PS- Ghazipur, was registered in connection with the accident. 3. In response to the notice of the petition, all the respondents appeared and filed their replies / written statements. 3(i). In the joint written statement filed by respondent Nos. 1 & 2 (in the capacity of the owner and driver respectively of Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-99XBT-4138), they have asserted that no accident has even been committed by the respondent No.2 at any point of time with Crane bearing registration No. HR-99XBT-4138 and police has falsely implicated the respondent No. 1 & 2 in the present matter. It is further averred that said vehicle is not involved in the alleged accident. It is further asserted that police officials of PS Ghazipur have obtained the signatures of the respondents on blank papers in the police station. It is further averred that the investigating officer has not conducted a fair investigation. It is further stated that respondents are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners. It is further stated that the respondent No. 2 had a valid driving licence. In the separate written statement filed by R1 (in the capacity of the owner-cum-driver of Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-55V-4780), it is stated that no accident has been committed at any point of time with the alleged vehicle bearing No.HR-55V-4780. It is further stated that police has falsely implicated R1 and he is not liable to pay any compensation and further that the said crane was duly insured on the date of accident and having other relevant documents i.e. fitness, permit, RC etc. and further that R1 had a valid driving licence. 3(ii). Respondent No.3 / insurer has filed its written statement and has taken defence that the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-99XBT-4138 was not holding any valid driving licence on the date of accident for driving the class of vehicle involved in the accident. It is further stated that crane bearing registration No. HR-55V-4780 was not having any valid permit and fitness certificate for use in the present case. It is stated that the permit was valid only for Haryana and the fitness was valid upto 02.03.2017, whereas the accident took place on 29.08.2017 and thus terms and conditions of the insurance policy have been willfully violated by the insured. It is further stated that owner and insurer of crane bearing registration No. HR-99XBT-4138 have not been made a party nor any document of the said vehicle has been filed in the DAR. It is further stated that as per DAR, the concrete slab slipped from HR-99XBT-4138 due to the negligence of Respondent No.2/Satender and due to the load of the slab, the other crane bearing registration No. HR-55V-4780 toppled, falling on the injured and thus the negligence was solely of the crane bearing registration No. HR-99XBT-4138. It is further averred that insurance company is not liable to pay compensation as vehicle bearing registration No. HR-55V-4780 was not responsible for the alleged accident, which was caused due to the sole negligence of the crane bearing registration No. HR-99XBT-4138. 4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed on 06.06.2019:- Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/ 2 (OPP) (iv)Relief. 5. In order to establish her claim, petitioner examined three witnesses. 5(i). Petitioner / PW1 deposed on the strength of affidavit Ex.PW1/A and deposed regarding manner of accident, injuries suffered by her and the medical expenses incurred on her treatment and relied upon the following documents:- Photocopy of driving licence and aadhar card of petitioner are Ex.PW1/1 (colly,2 sheets) (OSR) Attested copy of medical documents of the petitioner is Ex. PW1/2 (colly, 212 pages) Photocopies of academic documents of the petitioner are Ex. Computer generated salary slip of the petitioner is Ex.PW1/5 Photocopies of computer generated IRT of the assessment year 2017-18 alongwith PAN card are Ex. PW1/6 (colly, 6 sheets) PW2 Dr. Sanjeev Gambhir, Specialist Orthopedics, LBS Hospital, Khichripur, Delhi proved the disability certificate as Ex. PW2/A mentioning 93% permanent disability in relation to right upper limb. PW3, Sh. Akash Singh, Sr. Executive, Max Hospital, Patparganj, Delhi produced the treatment record of the petitioner and proved three discharge summaries of the petitioner Ex. PW3/A to Ex. PW3/C. Further, he also proved three final bills of the Max Hospital Ex.PW3/D, Ex. PW3/E and Ex. PW3/F. 19. According to her affidavit, after the accident, petitioner was first taken to Yashoda Hospital, Kaushambi Ghaizabad, and thereafter shifted to Max Hospital, Patparganj, Delhi. Her right hand elbow was operated upon and injury of the petitioner was diagnosed as crush injury right elbow with fracture, dislocation near total amputation with right distil ulna fracture with crush injury right index finger with right ILIAC wing fracture. In her affidavit attested on 31.01.2018, she stated that she could not recover and is having same problem in her right hand and further that she was on bed and her repeated dressing were being done at the hospital with no improvement shown and further that she was unable to resume her job. OPD consultation of Max hospital shows that she visited the hospital for treatment at least till 27.11.2017. The bill summary of Yashoda Hospital reflects that she was admitted there on 29.08.2017 and thereafter discharged on the same day. Further, the duplicate bill of Max Hospital shows that she was admitted to the hospital on 29.08.2017 and discharged on 15.09.2017. Further, another duplicate bill of Max Hospital shows that she was admitted on 19.09.2017 and discharged on 23.09.2017. In these circumstances, considering the nature of injuries suffered by petitioner, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs. 3,00,000/- to the petitioner under this head. CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 20. Thus, I deem it fit to grant a sum of Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner towards special diet. In her examination-in-chief Ex. PW1/A tendered on 30.05.2022 by way of affidavit attested on 31.01.2018, petitioner deposed that she is an MBA and at the time of accident, she was working with Parcel Now World Wide, a logistic startup and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
texts.arguments: For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/ 8 doing of the driver. It is an admitted case she was never thrown out of job and instead during the period of her treatment itself, the company where she was working had been shut down. Hence, there is no question of her re-joining the same job. There is nothing in the shape of medical documents to show that she was unable to take up new employment till September 2019 or that she made an effort to take up new job but due to the injuries sustained by her, she was declined a suitable job. There is no evidence led by the petitioner to suggest that the longevity of petitioner has been adversely affected due to the accident in question or that petitioner had any particular dream for future, which is shattered due to accident and there is absolutely no evidence to show any loss of expectation of life.

The issues are decided as follows:-
9.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.

Petitioner saw that the crane was in fallen down condition and the registration number of the crane which had fallen down on the right hand of the petitioner was HR-55V-4780.
R1/driver of the Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-55V-4780 examined himself in defence as R1W1.
He deposed in his cross-examination, admitting that his crane HR-55V-4780 had toppled and fallen down on the petitioner.
He also deposed that the contents of the FIR are wrong and that only one crane was carrying the slab.
He also disclosed that he is not aware what statement had been given by Rati Ram under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

Rati Ram is cited in the charge-sheet as an eye-witness but he was not examined either by the petitioner or by any of the respondents and hence, his version did not come on record during enquiry made by Tribunal.

His statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has purpose only to the extent of cross-examination to contradict him during his testimony before the Tribunal by putting his statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. to him, if there is any contradiciton

reflects that what he had stated to Police was that hydra crane yellow colour was bringing a concrete floor (iron contained) lying on road towards godown.

ISSUE No.2:
15.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
16. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July,

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though she may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent t

The next question that remains to be decided is the compensation with respect to the disability of the petitioner.

25. The disability certificate of LBS Hospital clearly shows that the petitioner is the case of 93%
disability in relation to right upper limb.
The doctor has been examined as PW2.
PW2 Dr. Sanjeev Gambhir has deposed that petitioner suffered permanent disability to the extent of 93% in relation to right upper limb and disability certificate Ex.PW2/A was issued in this regard.
The petitioner has not narrated how this disability will come in way of reducing the efficiency of the work in which the petitioner is engaged.

documents placed on record together with the testimony of the petitioner do not reflect any diminished salary post accident and there is nothing in her testimony to suggest that on account of the accident, there was any change in her job pr

from her employer as salary as on 06.09.2019 and further the said amount was consistently received by her in the year 2019.

Petitioner has not averred a word to suggest the nature of work done by her at work place and whether the was sitting or desk job or involved any active and consistent participation of use of her right upper limb, which was rendered incapab

Hence, a balanced approach has to be taken by the Tribunal.

Therefore, I am of the opinion that functional disability in relation to right lower limb of the petitioner must be considered as 30% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.

LIABILITY:
30.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.

As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured i.e.
the owner-cum-driver of Hydra Crane No. HR-55V-4780, the Insurance company/IFFCO TOKIO GIC is liable to compensate the third party.

The insurance company has examined a witness R3W1 to prove the objections raised by it and to prove that term or condition of insurance policy was breached/ violated by insured as the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and

It is not disputed that R1 did not have a valid permit to drive the crane in NCT of Delhi and had a local permit of Haryana and further that the offending vehicle Hydra Crane No.
Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon -
In my considered view, crane is a special vehicle and fitness of a crane should be ensured before driving such a special vehicle with a view to avoid any mishap.
In the case at hand, the mechanical defect in the crane is apparent.

Though R1 claimed in his cross-examination that Haryana Government stopped issuing fitness certificate to cranes before the date of accident and that no permit is required to drive a crane in Delhi, he did not lead any evidence to suggest t
R3W1 deposed that R1 did not have endorsement to drive a crane on his driving licence on the date of accident and the same was a requirement.

No suggestion was given to R3W1 that despite the offending vehicle in question being a category D vehicle with term excavator mentioned on the insurance certificate, still driver did not require an endorsement on the licence, giving authori
Further, offending vehicle did not have a permit to be taken to Delhi and was registered in Haryana, with a Haryana permit.
R1 failed to lead any evidence to suggest that permit was not required for a crane in Delhi but required in Haryana.

Hence, in my considered view, R3 has been successful in proving that the insured vehicle was used/plight without valid permit, valid driving licence and fitness certificate and hence, there was breach of general terms and conditions of insu
However, the breach in question is not such as would affect the right of third party, once it is established that vehicle was covered under the policy of insurance.
Law is well settled that insurance company would be entitled for recovery of the compensation amount from the registered owner/insured of the offending vehicle.

In case titled as Gurmeet Singh vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd & Ors, MAC App 288/2021 decided on 06.10.2023, it has been held that the respondent no. 3/ insurer is entitled to recover the compensation amount paid to the claimants.
In such circumstances, insurance company is entitled for recovery of the compensation amount from the respondent No.1 after paying the aforesaid compensation to the petitioner in the first place.

In view of above, it is held that respondent no.3/
insurer shall be liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.
